final.label: index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch

skill_entry.name: 14. A count, index or completion wait must cover the set it stands for
skill_entry.trigger: Added h/ or src/ lines: (a) A count (`v.size()`, `a * b`) bounds a loop or index into a compile-time-capacity member (`std::array<T, CAP>`, `T[CAP]`). (b) A `break` in an array-filling loop while a caller-read count (out-parameter or returned member) was set before the loop from the full input. (c) A helper's returned or out value starts as a sentinel (`0`, `nullptr`), is set in one arm of an explicit if/else or request-kind split, and its comment names the value. (d) A wait after a per-device loop names one device by a literal (`get_device(0)`) or carries a comment claiming it covers the loop. (e) A literal device index (`get_device(0)`, `(*pos_list_devices())[0]`) chooses a new object's device on a path every configuration runs.
skill_entry.procedure: (a) CAP from the struct; `git grep` every writer; from assignment to first indexed write record assert, clamp, return or NONE. (b) Each `break` path must reset the pre-loop count from the fill index; find its caller. (c) List out-value assignments with conditions; input classes from explicit branches or request kinds only; find a class that skips all and its consumer. (d) Read the function, the per-iteration callee (its device or queue) and the wait definition (what the completion check reads); compare the comment. (e) Grep other choosers of the object and tp2/tp4 aliases. For `<= (x / n) * n` evaluate at x = n; ask for a diag test. Grep replies for deferrals.
skill_entry.question: On every path, does this count, index or wait cover exactly the set it stands for (the array's capacity, every device the loop issued work to, the device this object binds to, the value its comment promises), and if not, which member is missed and who reads the result?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A count every writer asserts or clamps against CAP. A `break` path that resets the count from the fill index. A wait on the loop's last handle (PR 1722, silent), a one-queue loop whose comment names the member it ends on (PR 2008 'we always end on pdc 31'), or stated FIFO order. A sentinel the consumer tests before reading. A loop bound that is a model or device dimension. A `[0]` in a fake path or reading a property of an already-selected object. A line re-spelled from BASE. A written deferral: report once, accept. Token-index waits: concurrency check; two-count containers without compile-time capacity: state-ownership check. Never recompute kernel arithmetic, dispute CAP, run the test yourself, or block.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<count|index|wait>` at <file:line> comes from <source>, but <the array|the loop at :<line>|the object> is <capacity CAP | one transfer per device through `<callee>` | bound to one device>, and nothing between :<source> and :<use> ensures <count <= CAP | every device is waited | index 0 is right under TP2/TP4>. Wait only: the definition at <file:line> reads `<handle member>`, not its device argument, so N-1 devices are never waited; the comment at :<line> says '<quote>'. As is, <the caller `<fn>` reads the wrong `<count>` | we wait on `<member>` only>. <check `<count> <= CAP`? | wouldn't it be better to capture the device per iteration and wait on each? | perhaps a quick diag test with <boundary input>?>
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, with no label word; his own phrasings are an imperative ('something somewhere should ensure that `nshards` is <= `MAX_B`', 'check `work_req->nshards <= MAX_B`'), a fact-then-'As is' consequence with a two-alternative question ('wouldn't it be better to ... As is, we aren't actually waiting ...'), an endorsement of a bot finding that separates today's behaviour from the mechanism ('I do think there's merit to this complaint. Not sure it has to do with your current behavior ... but for sure ...'), and an admission plus a test ask when reading cannot settle it ('hard to truly analyze visually... perhaps a quick diag test would be worth it'). A relayed LLM item keeps the tool's own label ('**1. Low**'). He approved two of the four member PRs: PR 2011 at d4795f37a5 (2026-02-10T20:39:02Z, 28 minutes after the author's deferral reply) and PR 3008 at 17c6e0117d (2026-06-18T18:58:35Z). On PR 2233 he only commented (bham0n approved d634595662 on 2026-03-27; merged 2026-03-30 as merge commit 2bcd7f250e). PR 2287 is still open with no approval. Both PR 2011 sites were left unchanged at head with the author's written deferral. He never requested changes on any of the four.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk + full file at HEAD (the whole function around the loop, the wait or the helper) + other files (the struct that declares the array and its capacity constant; the definition of the wait call and the per-iteration callee that names the device or queue; the consumer of the out-value) + callers (the function that reads the out-parameter or the returned struct) + repository evidence of multi-device configurations (tp2/tp4 executor aliases in h/tron/models/common.hpp) + author replies (a written deferral). Runtime only as an ask to the author for an exact-boundary case; the reviewer does not run it.

## Check 14: a count, index or completion wait must cover the set it stands for

Setup addition (BASE for a PR whose base branch is not main, or that has merged): `BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`. `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself once the PR is merged into that branch, and `origin/main` gives a base weeks too old (PR 2011: 16aeb26d83 instead of ab75e61d83). Offline: the second parent's base from the PR's merge commit (`git -C WT log --format=%P -1 <merge commit>`) or the digest header. Note that an open PR's base.sha moves with the base branch (PR 2287 answers 9b6988c009 today; the review was run at 5f37572171).

Mapping a `-U0` diff hit to a HEAD line (the installed awk is mawk and rejects `match(s, re, arr)`; use python):
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > pr-u0.diff
python3 -I - < pr-u0.diff <<'EOF'
import re,sys
f=None;n=0
for i,l in enumerate(sys.stdin,1):
    m=re.match(r"^@@ -\S+ \+(\d+)",l)
    if l.startswith("+++ "): f=l[6:].strip()
    elif m: n=int(m.group(1))
    elif l.startswith("+"): print(i,f+":"+str(n)); n+=1
EOF
```
Read the row whose first number equals the grep line number (PR 2011: 350 -> h/pos/hwattention.hpp:645, 364 -> :674).

1. Candidates (five patterns) from the added lines of h/ and src/:
   (a) `grep -nE '^\+.*[a-z_]+ *= *[a-z_]+\.size\(\)|^\+.*(num|n)_?[a-z_]* *= *[0-9a-z_]+ \* [a-z_]+' pr-u0.diff`
       then `grep -nE 'std::array<[^>]*, *[A-Za-z_:0-9]+>|\[[A-Z_][A-Z_0-9]*\]' pr-u0.diff` for fixed-capacity members in the touched structs. Keep a count only when a later added loop, memcpy or index uses it against such a member; allocation sizes (`xferlen = a * b`) are not candidates.
   (b) `grep -nE '^\+\s*break;' pr-u0.diff` plus `grep -nE '^\+\s*(early_release|early_exit|release_early)\b' pr-u0.diff`; keep a hit only when the enclosing loop writes `arr[idx++]` or `arr[w_idx]` and a count set above the loop is read after it. Plain `return` statements of helpers are not candidates (42 hits over 12 silent diffs, all plain returns).
   (c) `grep -nE '^\+\s*(uint(8|16|32|64)_t|int|size_t|auto) +[a-z_]+ *= *(0|-1|nullptr|std::numeric_limits)[^x0-9]' pr-u0.diff`; drop struct default member initializers (the enclosing `@@` context names a `struct`) and default parameter values (the line ends with `)`, `,` or `) noexcept;`). Keep a hit only if the same function returns the name or stores it into a returned or by-reference struct: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<helper signature>/,/^}/' | grep -nE 'return .*<name>|\.<field> *= *<name>|return \{.*<name>'`.
   (d) `grep -nE '^\+\s*[a-zA-Z_:>.-]*(wait|join|flush|sync)[a-z_]*\([^;]*\);' pr-u0.diff | grep -vE '^[0-9]+:\+\s*(extern|inline|static|void|bool|int|auto)\b'` so that only call statements survive (declarations such as h/libpos.hpp:276 and definitions such as src/pos/driver.cpp:892 drop out). Keep a call whose device argument is a literal (`get_device(0)`, `devices[0]`) or that carries a coverage comment ("after the last xfer", "all devices"), and that sits after a loop over `get_num_devices()` or `pos_list_devices()`. A call whose argument is the loop's own last handle (`dev`, `xfer` assigned in every iteration) is not a candidate (do_not_fire, PR 1722). On PR 2011 this grep returns 3 call statements: the two Wade sites and src/pos/driver.cpp:1009 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(dev, xfer)` (one transfer, no loop; dropped).
   (e) `grep -nE '^\+.*(get_device\(([0-9]+|process_device_id\{[0-9]+\})\)|(devices|devs|instances|ranks|shards|queues)[a-z_]*(\(\))?\)*\[0\]|\.front\(\))' pr-u0.diff`. Drop a hit whose removed partner line exists at BASE with only the rename map applied (a re-spelling, check 10), a hit under a comment that defers the device choice in writing ("DEPRECATED", "next pass", "hardcodes devs[0]"), and a hit that reads a property of an object the code already selected (`job.incomplete_shards[0]->dev`, `saved_shards[0]->base_tok_ix`).
2. Pattern (a): `git -C WT show HEAD:<struct file> | grep -n -E '<array member>|<CAP>'` and `git -C WT grep -n '<CAP> *=' HEAD -- h` record the capacity. `git -C WT grep -n '<count> *=' HEAD -- h src` lists every writer. For each writer: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<assign line>,<first indexed write line>p' | grep -n -E 'TRON_ASSERT|<= *<CAP>|< *<CAP>|return'`; NONE = finding, one finding per shared array.
3. Pattern (b): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<loop start>,<loop end>p' | grep -n -E 'break;|return|<count> *='`; an exit with no `<count> = <fill index>` above it = finding. Caller: `git -C WT grep -n '<out-param>' HEAD -- src h`, then confirm the loops `for (wi = 0; wi < <count>; ...)` and the tail advances.
4. Pattern (c): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<helper signature>/,/^}/' | grep -n '<value> *='` lists the assignments with their enclosing `for`/`if`. Enumerate the caller's input classes from explicit branch conditions or request kinds only (PR 3008: attn_req true or false gives `num_metadata_wds > 0` or `== 0`); a loop bound that is a model dimension or a device property (n_kvheads, head_size, num_fetchers) counts as one class, never zero. A class that skips every assignment = finding. Consumer: `git -C WT grep -n '<stored field>' HEAD -- src h`; if every consumer tests a companion field before reading the value (driver.cpp:916 `if (xfer.readback_addr)` before `readback_value` at d4795f37a5), the sentinel is a designed absent value and not a finding. Old behaviour: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -n '<value>'`.
5. Pattern (d): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<function start>,<function end>p'`; record the loop set and the per-iteration call. Open the per-iteration callee (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<callee signature>/,/^}/'`) and record the device or queue it submits to (PR 2011: xfer_v_entry has `PosDevice* dev = devices[fpga_index];` and `hardware::xfer_blocks(dev, dev->load_weight_q, ...)`). `git -C WT grep -n -E 'void <wait fn>\(' HEAD -- src` and read which argument the completion check reads. State the covered set as the member whose handle the wait dereferences. Compare the comment above the wait with that set. Siblings: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n '<wait fn>(get_device'` (never grep the on-disk file: the worktree checkout is not at HEAD) and `git -C WT grep -n '<wait fn>(' HEAD -- h src`; report each sibling, linking the first.
6. Pattern (e): `git -C WT grep -n -E 'pos_list_devices\(\)|get_num_devices\(\)' HEAD -- h src` for the other choosers of the same object; `git -C WT grep -n -E 'using tp[24] = ' HEAD -- h/tron/models/common.hpp` for multi-device configurations; `git -C WT grep -n -E '<object>\(PosDevice\* dev' HEAD -- h` for the binding.
7. Exact-boundary loop bound: `grep -nE '^\+.*<= *\([a-z_]+ */ *[a-z_]+\) *\* *[a-z_]+' pr-u0.diff`; evaluate at x = n by hand; name the allocation site of the block at x; the remedy is a test ask, not a bug claim.
8. Author replies and deferrals: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.in_reply_to_id!=null) | [.user.login,.body] | @tsv' | grep -i -E 'next pass|upcoming PR|future|phase' | grep -v '\[bot\]'` (the word "phase" also hits a cursor[bot] reply on PR 2287). Offline: `grep -n -i -E 'reply by .*(next pass|upcoming PR|future|phase)' corpus/pr/tron-N.md`. A written deferral by the author or a branch contributor is reported once and accepted.

On PR 2011 (BASE ab75e61d83 from the GitHub base.sha, head d4795f37a5, base branch hwattention_sync): pattern (d) hits h/pos/hwattention.hpp:645 and :674 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(get_device(0), xfer)` after the loops at :635 and :666 `for (idx = 0; idx < get_num_devices(); idx++)` that call `xfer_v_entry(..., idx, ...)` at :640-641 and `xfer_k_entry` at :669-670; the literal `get_device(0)` and the comment at :643-644 'after the last xfer, wait for completion' are the trigger. src/pos/driver.cpp:892-893 declares dev `[[maybe_unused]]`; :899 `DmaQueue* q = xfer.queue;` and :912 `xfer.queue->check_xfer_complete(xfer.end_desc, xfer.end_wrap_count)` check completion through the handle; dev is read only in log strings (:903, :938, :980) and on the timeout diagnostic path (:954 `dev->hbm_kv_offset`, :958-961 `dev->hbm_map`/`dev->hbmw_map`, :975 `debug_exit(label, dev->idx)`), never in the completion check. So only the last device's transfer is waited and the first N-1 are not; Wade's 'first device' wording (2789792758) describes the dev argument, the mechanism misses N-1 devices either way. The handle is h/pos/device.hpp:185-202 `struct dma_xfer_state` (`queue` :187, `end_desc` :190, `end_wrap_count` :191). Author reply 2790051381 (mcherba): 'the next pass will make the calls device specific'; Wade approved 28 minutes later with both sites unchanged. Pattern (c) on this PR: src/pos/driver.cpp:796 `uint64_t readback_value = 0;` is assigned only under `readback_offset != 0xffffffff` (:797-800) and returned at :802, but the consumer at :916 reads it inside `if (xfer.readback_addr)`; not a finding (Wade's 2789831855 there only calls the `else` clause redundant). Pattern (a) hits only src/pos/fake.cpp `std::array<PosDevice*, MAX_DEVICES>` (fake path).
Negative controls for (d): PR 1722 (silent, 405d485e87) h/pos/hwattention.hpp:454 and :481 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(dev->idx, dev->load_weight_q, end_desc, curr_desc)` after `for (idx = 0; idx < get_num_devices(); idx++) { dev = devices[idx]; ... }` (last-handle wait, no coverage comment; driver.cpp:729-746 at that commit reads completion from the queue argument only, so devices 0..N-2 are not waited; Wade approved with no text). PR 2008 (silent, abe1dc19da) h/pos/hwattention.hpp:760 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(dev, dev->load_weight_q, end_desc, curr_desc)` after the per-fetcher loop :740-756 on one queue, :767 `wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete(fpga_index, 31, ...)` under the comment 'we always end on pdc 31' (approved with no text). Pattern (c) negative control: PR 1722 xfer_k_entry / xfer_v_entry `uint32_t end_desc = 0; uint32_t curr_desc = 0;` assigned inside one loop bounded by n_kvheads / num_fetchers (a model or device dimension, one class).
On PR 2233 (head af9438799a, merge-base de8081fac4; one commit above the merge base, the intermediate commits 2788a76c36, d634595662, df0bfaeb95, 4b7d03f71c are not objects in the worktree but `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=<commit>` serves them): pattern (a) writers src/pos/driver.cpp:449 and h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:634 (`nshards = ....size()`), array h/pos/device.hpp:91 `std::array<shard_layer_t, MAX_B>`, MAX_B = 32 at h/libpos.hpp:35; at head both writers assert (:454-456, :635-637) so the check does not fire; at 2788a76c36 driver.cpp:411 assigns and :414 loops with no assert between (the state Wade saw, 2982760463), and self_attention.hpp at d634595662 has no assert (3002034511). Pattern (b) src/pos/worker.cpp:807-808 `num_wcmds = 2 * nshards * num_acmds` (out-param :750), break at :1008 preceded by `num_wcmds = w_idx;` at :1006, callers :1279, :1331, :1602, :1607; worker.cpp at 2788a76c36 has no `num_wcmds = w_idx` (2983833171). Pattern 7: src/tron/gof.cpp:421-422 `base <= (tok_ix / shard_tokens) * shard_tokens` kept at head, no reply (3002297607). gof.cpp:413-415 'V is submitted after K on the same FIFO queue, so V completion implies K completion' is a context line in the PR 2233 diff, not an added line; it illustrates the stated-FIFO form but is untested as a Wade decision. On PR 3008 (BASE 8811bdd35f, pre-fix c68ea87f48, head 17c6e0117d): pattern (c) `uint32_t first_desc = 0;` (c68ea87f48 worker.cpp:1393), only assignment :1409 `if (mi == 0) first_desc = md_desc_idx;` inside the metadata loop, returned :1473, stored at :1486 `rx_entry.tx_desc_start_idx = first_desc;`; input classes from `num_metadata_wds > 0` (attn_req); fix 381ed8ed4a adds `if((act_num == 0) && (num_metadata_wds == 0)) first_desc = act_desc_idx;` (head :1428); contract comment :1371-1377.
On PR 2287 (BASE 5f37572171 at review time, head 1a88e897e1, open, no approval): pattern (e) hits h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1598 and :1623 `auto dev = (*pos_list_devices())[0];` (3029339639, 3029340601), plus `job.incomplete_shards[0]->dev` (model.hpp:1600) and `saved_shards[0]->base_tok_ix` which read a property of an already-selected object (dropped).
